title: Serving and Packaging PyTorch Models
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of serving and packaging pytorch models in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of serving and packaging pytorch models and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Serving and Packaging PyTorch Models: Inference loads a trained artifact, enters evaluation mode, preprocesses inputs, runs the model without unnecessary gradient tracking, and postprocesses outputs. Export adds a target-format compatibility boundary. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: A model becomes usable when callers can send validated inputs and receive stable outputs with known dependency, latency, and failure behavior. For this lesson, focus on model artifacts and dependencies and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Separate artifact loading from per-request inference; validate input size/type/range, avoid loading weights on every request, and verify exported outputs against eager execution. The source topics for this lesson are: Model artifacts and dependencies, A basic HTTP inference service, Input validation and request limits. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Call a reusable inference function on one item and a batch, then inspect output shape and error handling. Export is successful only if the target runtime supports the model’s operators and constraints. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

items.title: Model artifacts and dependencies
items.text: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.

items.text: Define the artifact/input/output contract and verify it end-to-end, including invalid input, runtime compatibility, and useful failure responses.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.py in a Python environment with a compatible PyTorch installation, then run `python example.py`. PyTorch snippets are not executed in the browser. For GPU- or package-specific snippets, install the matching supported dependencies first.

content.task: Try it yourself: Wrap a small model in a validated single/batch inference function and write one valid-input and one invalid-input test. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.
task_acceptance_criteria: The experiment demonstrates at least one relevant aspect of serving and packaging pytorch models.
Record the expected and observed result, including shape/dtype/device information when relevant.
Explain one common failure mode, compatibility limitation, or evaluation caveat.
hints: Begin with the smallest working example for serving and packaging pytorch models and keep input shapes explicit.
Change only one variable at a time; compare a tensor property, a printed value, or a test assertion.
Use the linked official reference for any hardware-specific, optional-package, or version-sensitive behavior.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not expose arbitrary file loading or accept unlimited request sizes in an inference endpoint.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.

summary: Serving and Packaging PyTorch Models belongs to the Export, Deployment, and Inference learning path.
Practice model artifacts and dependencies, a basic http inference service, input validation and request limits using the source-aligned checklist and read-example explanation.
Do not expose arbitrary file loading or accept unlimited request sizes in an inference endpoint.
